In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the hypothalami-pituitary- thyroid (HPT) axis and the hypothalamic neuropeptide systems in the regulation of energy balance.
the mechanisms of action of leptin on the hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis and the hypothalamo-thyroid axis, as well as the effects of leptin on food intake, energy expenditure, and body weight.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
leptin is the most important hormone in the hypothalamic regulatory system for the hypothalamic- pituitary-thyoid axis.
insulin and glucose are not essential mediators of leptin's effects on the hypothalamus and thyroid axis.
the central actions of insulin, glucose, and leptin on the hypothalami are not equivalent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leptin is the primary signal that regulates thyroid function during fasting.
central leptin is a key regulator of the thyroid axis during fasting, whereas insulin and glucose may have only limited roles in this process.
central leptin, but not central insulin or glucose, is essential in preventing fasting-induced suppression of hypothalamic TRH mRNA and circulating thyroid hormone levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
leptin is a more potent regulator of the hypothalmoic-pituitary axis than insulin and glucose.
the hypothalamic regulation of the thyroid axis during fasting is not as simple as previously thought.
the central effects of insulin and glucose on TRH gene expression are not sufficient to prevent the fasting-induced suppression of thyroid hormone levels.
